title: Prove a pivot-policy swap floor for the pivoted BIT fallback: at least 385 of 505 boundary children remain (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

#4235's paid pivoted BIT fallback uses a first-unit pivot rule and proves at most `s <= 2r` paid swaps, so at most `1+12r` children (505 at the retained `m = 64, r <= 42` boundary). Its open question 2 asks whether another pivot policy can reduce the swaps. This PR bounds how much any policy can gain:

```text
every pivot policy, diagonal suffix projector D_r:  s >= 2 min(r, m-r)   (attained)
m = 64, r <= 42, f >= 2: best policy's worst packet >= 385 children  (#4235: <= 505)
m = 64, r <= 42, f = 1:                              >= 129 children  (#4235: <= 169)
```

Claim type: **scoped proof with a finite certificate**. No new κ, no supplier admission, no audit of #4235 or #4100, and no change to the selected frontier. Package: `research/bit-pivot-policy-floor`. [Claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19081173).

## Result

The compiler family is #4235's: at stage `k` a policy may take **any** unit pivot in residual rows `k..m-1` and columns `0..m-1-k` of `M = P C`. A head swap is paid if the row is not `k` and a tail swap if the column is not `m-1-k`. Ordered clearing ADDs follow.

1. **Floor (proved).** On `D_r = diag(0^(m-r), 1^r)` every policy pays at least `2 min(r, m-r)` swaps. Zero rows and columns of `M` keep zero residual, and swaps only move zero labels out of the way of later stages. So each stage `k < min(r, m-r)` pays both a head swap and a tail swap.
2. **Attainment (proved).** An explicit policy pays exactly `2 min(r, m-r)`.
3. **Boundary consequence (proved).** For `r <= 32` the bound `s <= 2r` is sharp for every policy. Across `r <= 42`, a changed pivot policy can save at most 120 worst-case children (40 when `f = 1`), and only in ranks 33 to 42.
4. **Optimal-policy census (finite certificate).** Exhaustive optimal-policy search over all 142,070 idempotents in 13 complete `(q, m, r)` domains over F3 and F5. The worst case equals the floor except at corank one, where `s*(m, m-1) = 3` at `m = 4, 5, 6` (F3) and `m = 4` (F5), while the first-unit rule pays `2r` (up to 10). So the floor is not sharp above `m/2`, and a better rule does gain there.

## Evidence and reproduction

`verify.py` is standalone; #4235 is unmerged, so it reimplements the stage process. It checks each census count against `q^(r(m-r)) [m choose r]_q`, computes exact optimal and first-unit swap counts per idempotent, checks the suffix optimum equals the floor, runs the explicit policy and the first-unit rule on all 63 literal `m = 64` suffix fixtures, recomputes the boundary bills, and rejects a zero home pivot.

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-pivot-policy-floor
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/bit-pivot-policy-floor --check-source-history
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/bit-pivot-policy-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/bit-pivot-policy-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/bit-pivot-policy-floor/verify.py --extended   # opt-in, several minutes
```

Expected markers: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/bit-pivot-policy-floor outcome=completed`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` and `"status": "PASS_BIT_PIVOT_POLICY_FLOOR"`. Locally all four registered/package commands passed; each verify command took about 37 seconds. The opt-in run adds `m = 5`, ranks 2 and 3 over F3.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The floor holds for the declared compiler family and only for the projector `D_r`. A different normal form, pivot positions or swap pricing is outside it. The census optima are finite facts for the listed fields and sizes, not a formula. Whether the best policy reaches 385 at the boundary depends on `s*(64, r) <= 64` for `33 <= r <= 42`, which is open. No caller is built; preparation, routing and stock costs stay caller obligations as in #4235. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Determine `s*(m, r)` for `m/2 < r < m`. Is `s*(m, m-1) = 3` for every `m >= 4`? A bound `s* <= 2(m-r)+2` would make the best-policy boundary maximum exactly 385.
2. Find a polynomial-time pivot rule that attains `s*`. The home-first greedy rule is not optimal (10 against 3 at `m = 6, r = 5`).

## Related open work

- #4235 defines the compiler and proves `s <= 2r`. Its attained `2r` on suffix projectors agrees with this package's first-unit runs on all 63 `m = 64` fixtures; its `1+12r` = 505 and `1+4r` = 169 boundary bounds are recomputed here.
- #4237 counts children of the retained, unpivoted #4100 fallback program (33269 at `m = 64`). Different algorithm and bill; no shared number.
- #4215 checks #4100's good-packet normal form; not rerun here.

## CI notes

Both jobs passed on head `b55d08ec0`: `plan` and `replay (research/bit-pivot-policy-floor)` (2m22s). The opt-in `--extended` run is not registered in CI; it passed locally (882,090 idempotents for each of `m = 5`, `r = 2, 3` over F3, optimal worst case 4 in both, equal to the floor).
